Validating rtfreporter in your environment

Source: vignettes/articles/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd

A company that uses R for clinical reports validates each package for its own use, in its own environment. rtfreporter gives you two things for that: its own quality records, and templates for yours.

What the package provides

The package keeps three records of what it does and how it is tested.

  • Functional Requirements (FR). One row per thing a function does, an argument, a data shape it handles, a misuse it stops, or a risky combination. Each has an id such as FR-PL161. They are in inst/validation/requirements.csv.
  • Functional Tests (FT). The package’s tests, each mapped to the FRs it checks by a person who read it.
  • The Traceability Matrix (FR -> FT). Every FR with its tests. An FR with no test is listed as a deviation, with its risk and why it is accepted.

At each release, CI writes the Quality Report: the results on every environment (six in CI – Linux, macOS and Windows, several R versions – and two runs on the maintainers’ PC), the deviations, the conclusion and how to read each attachment. It is attached to the GitHub release with its evidence: the Traceability Matrix (traceability-<tag>.xlsx), every environment’s sessionInfo and test log (environments-<tag>.txt), the mapped tests’ log and the tables behind the results. Only the report of a published release can conclude validation-ready; a report made any other way is marked DRAFT. The rules behind it are the package’s Quality Plan (inst/validation/quality-plan.md, also in the kit below).

You use these as supplier evidence. You do not repeat them.

What you do

  1. Copy the kit into a folder of your own.

    library(rtfreporter)
rtfreporter_validation_kit("rtfreporter-validation")

    The folder holds:

    File What it is
    validation_plan.md The Validation Plan: scope, intended use, roles, approach, acceptance criteria, deviations.
    urs.csv, urs.md The User Requirement Specification (URS): your requirements (UR-NNN), each linked to FR ids. urs.md explains the columns of the URS and of the UAT cases.
    uat_cases.csv, uat_cases.xlsx Your user acceptance test (UAT) cases (UAT-NNN) on dummy data, with columns to record the results.
    build_user_matrix.R Writes your Traceability Matrix (URS -> FR -> UAT).
    validation_summary_report.md The Validation Summary Report you fill at the end.
    quality-plan.md, requirements.csv The package’s Quality Plan and FRs, for reference.

    The examples are fictional (a company called “Example Pharma”). Replace them with yours.

  2. Write the Validation Plan. Say which version, which environment and what use. Decide how deeply to test each priority.

  3. Adapt the URS. Keep the needs your reports have, drop the others, add your own. For each, find the FRs it relies on in requirements.csv (filter on the function you call).

  4. Run the UAT cases in your environment, on dummy data. Record what you saw, the result, who and when. A failure is a deviation: record it, find its cause, and decide (the Validation Plan, section 6).

  5. Build the matrix.

    kit_dir <- "rtfreporter-validation"
source(file.path(kit_dir, "build_user_matrix.R"))

    Or from a shell, in the folder that holds the kit: Rscript rtfreporter-validation/build_user_matrix.R rtfreporter-validation. It writes user_traceability.csv and user_traceability.xlsx into the kit folder.

  6. Fill the Validation Summary Report, and attach the package’s Quality Report for the same version.

How they connect

The FR ids join your records to the package’s.

your need          the package's requirement      the package's tests
UR-008  ----------> FR-PL161 decimal alignment ----> FT (in traceability.xlsx)
   |
   +--> UAT-011  your check in your environment
  • Your matrix (URS -> FR -> UAT) shows that every need has a check of your own.
  • The package’s matrix (FR -> FT) and Quality Report show that the same FRs are tested, and passed, on every environment of its Quality Plan.
  • Together they cover a need from your words down to a test.

A new version

Read the version’s NEWS and the release’s records. Find the FRs added, changed or removed. Rerun the UAT cases that name them, and the high-priority ones. Write a short Validation Summary Report for the new version (the Validation Plan, section 8).
